profile: SQLite 3.47.2 with the ordinary-table, numbered-parameter and scalar roles already defined for the checked SQLite profile.
scope: Unqualified truth words and the Boolean interpretation of the right operand of IS and IS NOT.

TruthTest.role: The resolved comparison of one scalar's Boolean value to true or false
TruthTest.conditions: The checked scalar scope owns all descendants and bounds. Both Boolean attributes are closed.
TruthTest.meaning: Convert the operand through SQLite Boolean conversion. A NULL result matches neither required truth value. Produce INTEGER 1 for a match and INTEGER 0 otherwise, complemented when requested.
TruthTest.externalInterpretation: The same bound values, column scopes and SQLite truth conversion apply.
TruthTest.sql: Emit a searched CASE yielding integer 0 or 1. Use the operand directly as the condition for true and logical NOT for false. Complement the two explicit results for the negated test. Register the operand once and avoid truth-word lookup in the emitted statement.

admission: Resolve TRUE and FALSE as a column name when the checked analysis facts bind it to a visible ordinary column. Treat it as INTEGER 1 or 0 in ordinary scalar roles when no such name applies.
For IS, IS NOT, IS NOT DISTINCT FROM and IS DISTINCT FROM, a right-hand truth word resolved as a constant triggers Boolean comparison. Redundant grouping does not change this role.
An explicit unary plus on the right is an ordinary numeric expression. A right-hand resolved column named true or false also keeps ordinary NULL-safe comparison.
Unknown or unsupported name bindings cannot publish a completed value.
observations: INTEGER 0 and 1 for truth tests, exact NULL-safe equality for shadowed columns, integer storage for truth constants, the same labels and numbered binding registration.
Different results for 7 IS TRUE and 7 IS +TRUE. NULL matches neither truth value and both complemented tests succeed.
An explicit truth-test value remains a truth test when its input relation exposes columns named true or false.

finite.identity: Recover root, requested truth, negation, and operand identity from constructed values. Exhaust all 80 combinations.

exploration.structure: Generate nested truth tests under both root forms, with NULL, numeric and nonnumeric data, compound scalar operands and repeated parameter slots.
